text:
Thomas Chabot is still Ottawa's minutes leader on the back end at 23 and a half a night, and the Senators are winning plenty of those minutes. At five on five they get about 57% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, close to five points better than without him.

The points have come almost entirely as assists: 2 goals and 10 helpers in 19 games, one of the goals into an empty net against Pittsburgh. His on-ice numbers ride a lot of good fortune, with teammates finishing well above their chances when he's out there, so the plus side of his line may soften. The process underneath is steady. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 2.0 wins last season, 29th among defensemen, nearly all of it from even-strength offense, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him stopping 16% of entries at his blue line against a typical 11%.

One thing to keep an eye on: CBS Sports flagged him as potentially injured on Nov. 18, though he played the next night against Philadelphia. His ice time over the last ten games is down about three and a half minutes from his season pace.
